extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO applicants, administrative-law attorneys, and pro se litigants
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing USPTO denial/suspension of registration to practice (OED actions) and the courts' review of those decisions, including service-of-process and appellate-review rules. Focuses on candor disclosures on registration applications, regulatory provisions (37 C.F.R.), and applicable statutory/administrative review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO statutory authority to suspend/exclude under 35 U.S.C. § 32
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO has statutory authority to suspend or exclude from further practice before the PTO any person shown to be incompetent or disreputable, guilty of gross misconduct, or who does not comply with the regulations established under section 2(b)(2)(D) of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory authority supports OED actions to deny or suspend registration; such agency determinations are subject to review under the Administrative Procedure Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Procedure Act (APA) standard of review
rubrics_metrics.description: A court shall set aside the USPTO's determination if it is 'arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law.' (5 U.S.C. § 706(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of an agency's final order is governed by the APA standard; appellate courts reapply the APA standard when reviewing district-court judgments in petitions for review of USPTO registration decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of review for procedural rulings on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Dismissals under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 12(b)(5) (improper service) are reviewed for abuse of discretion under regional-circuit law; decisions granting summary judgment are reviewed de novo under regional-circuit law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellate review follows regional-circuit standards (Fourth Circuit in this case) for procedural and merits determinations; cite Shao, Villa, and Syngenta precedents as authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of process constraints (Fed. R. Civ. P. 4(c)(2) and 4(i)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 4(c)(2) prohibits a party to the underlying lawsuit from serving the complaint and summons. Rule 4(i)(2) requires that when serving the United States (or agency) a copy of the summons and complaint be sent by registered or certified mail to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with these rules (e.g., personally serving an agency-defendant or failing to send required certified/registered mail) can justify dismissal for improper service; local rules (e.g., E.D. Va. Local Rule 83.5) do not excuse noncompliance with Rule 4(i)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.7(h)(4) applies to individuals who were 'disbarred or suspended from practice of law or other profession, or [who] ha[ve] resigned in lieu of a disciplinary proceeding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation does not apply to applicants who were not disbarred or suspended and who did not resign in lieu of discipline; determining applicability is a threshold legal question for the agency/district court.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED fact-gathering under 37 C.F.R. § 11.8(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED may request information from relevant persons (e.g., supervisors) regarding an applicant's moral character and reputation pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.8(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED's inquiries can lead to discovery of disciplinary actions (e.g., suspensions) and prompt the agency to request additional information from the applicant about the nature and circumstances of such events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candor and truthfulness requirement on USPTO registration applications (Question 17 & exhortation to candor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications contain a prefatory 'exhortation to candor' and specific candor/truthfulness questions. Question 17 asks: 'Have you ever been disciplined, reprimanded, or suspended in any job for conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, misrepresentation, deceit, or for any violation of Federal or State laws or regulations?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answering 'no' to such questions while omitting a recent suspension (e.g., for being paid for hours not worked) can support an agency finding of lack of candor and justify denial of registration. Applicants should disclose relevant disciplinary actions with explanation to comply with the exhortation to candor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight and relevance of letters of recommendation/credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation and credentials may be submitted by applicants to support fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency may reasonably conclude that such letters are unresponsive to a specific candor/disclosure issue; the presence of favorable recommendations does not override or negate a failure to disclose material disciplinary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence basis for disciplinary/suspension decisions (agency factfinding)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may base suspension on a detailed analysis of the underlying facts (for example, detailed analysis of time worked and unaccounted-for time supporting an AWOL finding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credible, document-based agency factfinding supporting misconduct findings will not be overturned as arbitrary or capricious absent a legal error; the substance of the agency's factual analysis matters in reviewing the final order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-on-appeal limitation (Ballard Med. Prods. v. Wright rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellate court may consider only the record as it was made before the district court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials or pages not presented to the district court should be stricken or not considered on appeal; litigants must ensure relevant evidence is in the district-court record to preserve it for appellate review.
